# Contract: module manifest, `renox.toml [modules]`, `renox.lock`

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Version | **1.4** (F7, #503: `[optional_dependencies]`; rules MF5 and MF8 amended). 1.3 (F7, #346: `permissions.app_access`, `renox.toml [modules].<name>.app_tables`, the lock's `approved.app_access` and `approved.app_tables`; rule MF16; for `ops.md` 1.8.0). 1.2 (F7, #318: `registry:` sources, `[publisher]`, the `module.sig` file, `[storage]`, `price`; the lock's `key_id`, `signature`, and `approved_version`; `renox publish`; the `isolate` mode taking effect; rule MF15; for `artifact.md` 1.4). 1.1 (F5, #272: `[authz.ownership]`, `[authz.entities]`, `[authz.default_roles]`, `[authz] sensitive`, `[realtime.feeds]`, `[[tools]]` carried, `permissions.roles` and `approved.roles`, the `auth.principal` convention, `renox.toml [authz]` and `[realtime]`; rules MF13–MF14). 1 (F4, #225) is the first version. History: "Changelog" at the bottom |
| Producers | Module authors write `module.toml`; tenants write `renox.toml [modules]`; `cli/` (P11) writes `renox.lock` (`renox add`, `renox install`, `renox approve`, #235) |
| Consumers | `cli/` (P11): resolves, approves, checks, and copies the lock into the artifact's `modules` field (`artifact.md` section 3, #227); the module broker in `crates/renox-runtime` and `crates/renox-cell` (P9, #230, #231): enforces what the lock approved, through the artifact; `sdk/` (P10, #236): generates `renox-modules.d.ts`; every official module (`modules/*`, #237–#239) |
| Machine-readable | [`schemas/module-manifest.schema.json`](schemas/module-manifest.schema.json) (root: `module.toml`; `$defs/renoxToml`: `renox.toml`), [`schemas/renox-lock.schema.json`](schemas/renox-lock.schema.json) (JSON Schema draft 2020-12, applied to the parsed TOML) |
| Examples | [`examples/manifest/`](examples/manifest/): single files and whole projects (section 8) |
| Checker | `bun run docs/contracts/validate.ts` (schemas, examples, rules MF1–MF16) |
| Sources | `docs/10-modules.md` (the module system), `docs/18-build-plan.md` (catalog, definition of done for a module), `docs/13-decisions.md` D12 (isolation modes), D14 (outbox), D17 (forward-only migrations, versioned views), `docs/06-data.md` (authorizer and prefixes), `docs/24-threat-model.md` (module publisher boundary) |

A module is a mini app with the same folder structure as an app (`docs/10-modules.md`). Its `module.toml` says what it is, what it needs, and what it offers. A tenant installs modules in `renox.toml [modules]`; the CLI resolves them, asks the tenant to approve their permissions, and records the result in `renox.lock`. The lock is the only input the artifact takes from this contract: what the runtime enforces is what the tenant approved, never what a manifest asks for later.

All three files are TOML. The schemas validate the document a TOML parser produces (`Bun.TOML.parse` in `validate.ts`), so a TOML table is a JSON object and an array of tables is an array.

## 1. Files

| File | Written by | Where | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `module.toml` | module author | root of the module tree (`modules/<name>/module.toml`, or a `path:`/`git:` source) | Section 2 |
| `renox.toml` `[modules]` | tenant | app root | Section 4. The other sections of `renox.toml` belong to the CLI and to `artifact.md` |
| `renox.lock` | CLI | app root, committed with the app | Section 5. Never edited by hand: `renox check` refuses a lock that does not match (MF12) |
| `module.sig` | `renox publish` (1.2) | root of a module tree published to the registry | Section 5, "Registry modules". Not part of the module tree hash |

Generated from these files and defined elsewhere:

- `renox-modules.d.ts` (#236): the types of `renox:modules` and `ctx.services` for the app and each module, from `[exports.services]` and the services' TypeScript signatures (`ops.md` 1.3.0, #226).
- The artifact's `modules` field (#227, `artifact.md` section 3): the lock entries, in lock order, with each module's exports.

## 2. `module.toml`

Abridged from [`examples/manifest/module.billing.valid.toml`](examples/manifest/module.billing.valid.toml) (the manifest of `docs/10-modules.md`):

```toml
[module]
name = "billing"
version = "1.2.0"

[dependencies]
auth = "^1.0"
org  = "^1.0"

[config]
provider = { type = "enum", values = ["stripe", "checkout", "telr", "paytabs", "ngenius"] }
currency = { type = "string", default = "AED", max_length = 3 }

[permissions]
tables  = "billing__*"
network = ["api.stripe.com", "secure.telr.com"]
secrets = ["BILLING_PROVIDER_KEY"]
slots   = ["admin.sidebar"]
roles   = ["finance", "viewer"]                  # 1.1: the roles the module may assign

[exports]
views = ["billing__public_user_plans_v1"]

[exports.services]
getActivePlan = "The user's active plan, or null"

[exports.events."billing.invoice_paid"]
payload = { type = "object", required = ["invoice_id", "user_id"], properties = { invoice_id = { type = "string" }, user_id = { type = "string" } } }

[imports]
services = ["auth.currentUser", "org.currentOrg"]

[[slots]]
name = "admin.sidebar"
template = "partials/admin-menu.html"
requires = "invoice.read"

[[tools]]
name = "create_invoice"
file = "tools/create-invoice.ts"
action = "invoice.create"

[authz]
actions   = ["invoice.read", "invoice.create", "invoice.refund"]
sensitive = ["invoice.refund"]                   # 1.1: audited, and the Renox::Action::"sensitive" group

[authz.ownership]                                # 1.1: db.scoped()
"billing__invoices" = { owner = "user_id", org = "org_id" }

[authz.entities]                                 # 1.1: Cedar entity Billing::Invoice
Invoice = { table = "billing__invoices", attrs = ["amount", "org_id", "status"] }

[authz.default_roles]                            # 1.1
finance = ["invoice.read", "invoice.refund"]
viewer  = ["invoice.read"]

[realtime.feeds]                                 # 1.1: the change feed
"billing__invoices" = "invoices:{org_id}"
```

No other tables or keys are allowed at any level (`additionalProperties: false`), so a typo can never silently drop a permission or an export.

### `[module]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, no `__`, no trailing `_`, not `app`, `renox` or `authz` (MF1) | yes | The module's name **and its table prefix** `<name>__`. `app` is the tenant's own code (`artifact.md` section 1); `renox` is the platform (`renox__*` tables); `authz` is the platform's event namespace (`authz.roles_changed`, #272). The catalog name in `docs/18-build-plan.md` may differ where it is not a valid name: `gcc-data` is installed as `gcc` (tables `gcc__*`), `2fa` as `twofa` |
| `version` | semver `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-pre]`, no build metadata | yes | The version of this tree. Public API changes follow semver (`docs/10-modules.md`, rule 3) |
| `isolation` | `"shared"` \| `"isolate"` | no, default `"shared"` | D12. The least isolation the module accepts; a tenant may raise it, never lower it (MF11). `shared`: one context with the app and other modules; `isolate`: its own isolate with its own heap limit, serialised service calls, and only its approved secrets (`ops.md` 1.7.0, section 15.6; runs from #320) |
| `description` | string, ≤ 200 | no | One line for `renox add` and the dashboard |
| `price` | `{ amount, currency, period }` (1.2) | no | Informational, shown by the registry and `renox add`: `amount` a decimal string (`"49.00"`), `currency` ISO 4217 (`"AED"`), `period` `"once"`, `"month"`, or `"year"`. Nothing is charged through it in F7 (payouts are an owner decision, `docs/15`) |

### `[publisher]` (1.2)

Required in a tree published with `renox publish`; ignored for `path:` and `git:` sources.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}$` | The registry publisher; `registry:<publisher>/<name>` names the module (section 4). Claimed once in the registry, never reused |
| `key_id` | `ed25519:<base64url of the 32-byte public key, no padding>` | The publisher's signing key. The registry lists a publisher's keys; a revoked key fails MF15 at install |

### `[storage]` (1.2)

`allowed_types`: the content types the module's `ctx.storage.put` accepts (`ops.md` section 21), MIME `type/subtype` without parameters, at most 64. Absent: the platform defaults (`artifact.md` 1.4, "Storage, AI, and the SBOM"). Copied to the artifact's module entry as `storage`.

### `[dependencies]`

Module name → semver range. A dependency is required for service calls and public views, and only for those (`docs/10-modules.md`, "Five communication mechanisms"): events, hooks, and slots need none. Every dependency must itself be installed in `renox.toml` (MF5); the CLI never installs a module implicitly. A module that is only wanted when present goes in `[optional_dependencies]`.

Ranges are a fixed subset of npm's:

| Form | Matches | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `^X.Y.Z` (also `^X.Y`, `^X`) | `>= X.Y.Z` and below the next change of the left-most non-zero part | `^1.2` = `>=1.2.0 <2.0.0`; `^0.3` = `>=0.3.0 <0.4.0`; `^0.0.4` = `=0.0.4` |
| `~X.Y.Z` (also `~X.Y`, `~X`) | `>= X.Y.Z` and below the next minor (the next major for `~X`) | `~1.2.3` = `>=1.2.3 <1.3.0` |
| `X.Y.Z` or `=X.Y.Z` | exactly that version | `1.0.0` |
| `>=A <B` (full versions, one space) | the interval | `>=1.2.0 <1.5.0` |

A pre-release version (`1.3.0-rc.1`) satisfies only an exact range naming it. Nothing else (`*`, `||`, `x`, hyphen ranges) is accepted.

### `[optional_dependencies]` (1.4)

Module name → semver range, with the same range forms as `[dependencies]`. When the module is installed, its version must satisfy the range (MF2) and it is ordered before this one; when it is not installed, nothing is required and the module still builds. Only hooks may be used from an optional dependency: a hook `<dep>.<name>` in `permissions.hooks` is allowed when `<dep>` is an optional dependency, and the fill is ignored while `<dep>` is not installed (MF8). Services and views still need `[dependencies]` (MF7 is unchanged). A name may not appear in both tables (MF5). The lock's `dependencies` lists the required names only.

### `[config]`

Key (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`) → declaration. The tenant sets values in `renox.toml`; the module reads the resolved object as `ctx.config` (`ops.md` 1.3.0, #226).

| Field | Applies to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | all | `"string"`, `"enum"`, `"int"` (64-bit, within ±(2^53 − 1)), `"bool"` |
| `values` | `enum` only, required there | Allowed strings, unique, 1–64 |
| `default` | all | Must have the key's type and pass its bounds (MF10) |
| `required` | all | Default: `true` when there is no `default`, else `false`. `required = true` together with a `default` is rejected (MF10). An optional key without a default is absent from `ctx.config` when unset |
| `min`, `max` | `int` only | Inclusive bounds, `min ≤ max` |
| `max_length` | `string` only | Characters, 1–4096; without it a string value is at most 4096 characters |
| `description` | all | One line |

Secrets are never config: a value that must stay secret is a secret name under `[permissions]`, set with `renox secrets set`.

### `[permissions]`

What the module asks the tenant to approve (section 3). Every key is optional; an absent key asks for nothing.

| Key | Type | Meaning | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tables` | exactly `"<name>__*"` (MF4) | The module owns tables, views, indexes, and triggers named `<name>__…` and may write them. Absent: the module has no tables and no migrations | SQLite authorizer (`docs/06-data.md`); `artifact.md` V19 |
| `network` | allowlist entries, syntax of `ops.md` section 2 | Hosts the module's `fetch` may reach. Separate from the app's `[fetch] allow` and from every other module's | `op_fetch` with the module's list (`ops.md` 1.3.0, #226) |
| `secrets` | names `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` that start with `<NAME>_`, the module name in upper case (MF4) | The secrets the module reads as `ctx.secrets`. The prefix keeps one module from asking for the app's or another module's secret by name | `op_secrets_get_all` (`ops.md` section 3), once per module from 1.3.0 (#226) |
| `slots` | slot names | The slots the module fills; must be exactly the names of its `[[slots]]` (MF8) | Renderer slot registry (`artifact.md` section 3) |
| `hooks` | hook names | The hook points the module fills from `hooks.ts`; each must be exported by another installed module (MF8). A filler can halt another module's flow (`auth.after_login`), so filling is approved | Broker (`ops.md` 1.3.0, #226) |
| `roles` (1.1) | role names, exactly the keys of `[authz.default_roles]` (MF13) | The roles the module may assign with `ctx.authz.roles.assign` (`ops.md` section 17). Assigning a role grants what its policies permit, so it is approved; any other role rejects with `RENOX_MODULE_UNDECLARED` | `op_authz_roles_*` (`ops.md` 1.5.0, #279) |
| `app_access` (1.3) | `"read"` \| `"write"` | Access to the app's own `app__*` tables that the app grants this module by name in `renox.toml` (`app_tables`, section 4). `read`: `SELECT`; `write`: `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`. Never DDL, never a table the app did not name, never another module's tables. Every write is audited (`ops.md` section 1, "App tables"). Absent: the module cannot touch any `app__*` table, whatever the app grants (MF16) | SQLite authorizer (`ops.md` 1.8.0 section 1) |

Reading another module's public view needs no permission: it follows from `[dependencies]` and `[imports]` (MF7), and the authorizer allows `SELECT` on `<dep>__public_*` for declared dependencies only. Defining actions, entities, owned tables, and feeds (`[authz]`, `[realtime]`) needs no permission either: they concern the module's own tables and resources (MF14), and a policy that grants an action still comes from the app's or the module's policy set.

**App tables (1.3).** A module that works on the app's data (a reports module, an admin panel, an import tool) asks for `app_access`; the app decides which of its tables the module sees. Both halves are needed: the module's request (`app_access`, approved like every permission) and the app's grant (`app_tables`, named one by one, no wildcard). The lock records both (section 5), and the runtime enforces the lock.

### `[exports]`

The module's public API, versioned with `version` (`docs/10-modules.md`, rule 3).

| Key | Shape | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `views` | `["<name>__public_<id>_v<n>"]` | Views the module creates in its migrations for dependants (D17). `<name>` is this module (MF6); `<id>` matches `[a-z0-9_]+`; `v<n>` starts at `v1` |
| `services` | `{ <export name> = "<one-line doc>" }` | Named exports of `services.ts`. The name is a JavaScript identifier; the signature comes from the TypeScript source (#236) |
| `events` | `{ "<name>.<event>" = { payload = <schema>, description? } }` | Events the module emits. The name starts with this module's name (MF6). The payload schema is JSON Schema with the keyword subset of `validate.ts` (`README.md`, "Checking"); `op_events_emit` validates against it (`ops.md` 1.3.0, #226) |
| `hooks` | `{ "<name>.<hook>" = { args = <schema>, result? = <schema>, description? } }` | Hook points the module runs with `ctx.hooks.run`. Same naming and schema rules as events (MF6) |

### `[imports]`

What the module uses from its dependencies, so a broken contract shows up in `renox check` before any code runs (`docs/23-failure-modes.md`, "Module contract broken on upgrade").

| Key | Shape | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `services` | `["<dep>.<service>"]` | Each `<dep>` is in `[dependencies]`, and the installed version of `<dep>` exports `<service>` (MF7) |
| `views` | `["<dep>__public_<id>_v<n>"]` | Each view's prefix is a dependency that exports it (MF7) |

`renox check` (#235) compares `[imports]` with the code: every `renox:modules` member a module calls and every `<dep>__public_*` name in its SQL must be listed. The app has no manifest; it may use every installed module's exports.

### `[[slots]]`

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | slot name | The `<r-slot name>` this module fills (rendered by another module's or the app's template) |
| `template` | `partials/….html` in the module tree | The partial inserted. Must exist in the module tree (MF9) |
| `requires` | action name | The authorization action a user needs for the content to render. Must be in `[authz].actions` (MF9). Evaluated from F5; carried from F4 |
| `priority` | integer 0–1000, default 100 | Order among the fillers of one slot: lower first, ties by module name |

### `[[tools]]`

MCP tools (`docs/20-ai-agents-mcp.md` section 2; `ops.md` section 19): `name` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`), `file` (`tools/….ts` in the module tree, MF9), `action` (in `[authz].actions`, MF9), `confirm` (default `false`), `description`. From 1.1 they are **carried in the artifact** as `tool` routes (`artifact.md` 1.3): `renox build` reads the `tool(...)` the file default-exports, records its input schema, and takes `name`, `action`, `confirm`, and `description` from the manifest, which must equal the file's (`renox check`, #284). Tool names are unique across the app and its installed modules (`artifact.md` V25).

### `[authz]`

The module's side of `docs/11-authorization.md` (`ops.md` section 17). Everything here names the module's own tables and resources (MF14); the policies that grant actions live in `policies/*.cedar`, carried in the artifact (`artifact.md` section 1), and are evaluated from F5.

| Key | Shape | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `["<resource>.<verb>"]` | The actions the module defines. `slots[].requires`, `tools[].action`, `sensitive`, and the actions of `default_roles` name them (MF9, MF13) |
| `sensitive` (1.1) | a subset of `actions` (MF13) | Decisions on these actions are audited in `renox__authz_audit`, and the merged schema puts them in the group `Renox::Action::"sensitive"` (`docs/11`: "requires MFA, audit-logged") |
| `[authz.ownership]` (1.1) | `"<table>" = { owner = "<column>", org? = "<column>" }`, tables under `<name>__` (MF14) | The owned tables `db.scoped()` fences: `owner` is the user (or session) column, `org` the organisation column. Module code reaching an owned table without a scope is refused (`RENOX_DB_SCOPE`) |
| `[authz.entities]` (1.1) | `<Type> = { table? = "<name>__…", id? = "<column>", attrs = ["<column>", …] }`, `<Type>` matching `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$` | The Cedar entity types of the module, `<Module>::<Type>` with `<Module>` the module name capitalised: `attrs` are the only attributes sent to the engine; `table` (own prefix, MF14) and `id` (default `id`) let the cell load a `guard` resource |
| `[authz.default_roles]` (1.1) | `<role> = ["<action>", …]`, actions of the merged action set (MF13) | The roles the module ships; its default policies grant them these actions. `permissions.roles` lists exactly these role names (MF13), and the lock's `approved.roles` is the tenant's approval |

**The `auth.principal` convention (1.1).** The `auth` module (#291) exports the service `auth.principal(sessionId)` and the hook point `auth.principal` (`[exports.hooks."auth.principal"]`, `args = { principal }`). The cell calls the service once per request (`ops.md` section 17, "Principal"); the service builds the principal from its own tables and runs the hook, whose fillers extend `principal.attrs` and return `undefined` (a filler that halts is treated as a throw): `2fa` sets `attrs.mfa_verified`, `org` sets `attrs.org`. A module that wants an attribute on the principal fills this hook (`permissions.hooks = ["auth.principal"]`, approved at install like any hook fill); nothing else may add to a principal. `auth` also exports `auth.verifyAgentToken` for `/mcp` (`ops.md` section 19, #286).

### `[realtime]` (1.1)

`[realtime.feeds]`: `"<table>" = "<topic pattern>"`, tables under `<name>__` (MF14), the pattern a topic (`ops.md` section 18) whose `{column}` placeholders name columns of that table (`artifact.md` V26 checks the table against the module's migrations). After a commit that changes the table, the cell publishes `{ table, rowid, op }` to the topic to the connections that passed the subscribe check.

## 3. Permissions and approval

- **At install** (`renox add <module>`) and at every upgrade, the CLI shows the module's `[permissions]` and asks the tenant to approve them. The approved set is written to the module's lock entry as `approved` (section 5).
- **A changed request needs a new approval.** When a manifest's `[permissions]` differ from its lock entry's `approved` in any way (a host added, a secret removed, a hook filled), `renox check` and `renox build` fail with MF12 until the tenant runs `renox approve <module>`. Removing a permission also needs approval, so the lock always says exactly what runs. `docs/23-failure-modes.md`, "Marketplace module unsigned or permission diff on upgrade", is the F7 registry form of the same rule.
- **What runs is what was approved.** The artifact copies `approved`, not the manifest's request (`artifact.md` V22), and the runtime enforces the artifact (`ops.md` 1.3.0, #226). A module that asks for more after approval gets nothing more until the tenant approves.
- **Approval in the control plane.** The control plane records the artifact's module permissions as approved at upload, as it does for the app's (`deploy-api.md` section 4, "Outcomes"). Dashboard approval of module upgrades is F7.

## 4. `renox.toml [modules]`

```toml
[modules]
auth    = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/auth" }
org     = { version = "^1.0" }
billing = { version = "^1.2", mount = "/billing", config = { provider = "telr" } }
acme    = { version = "^0.4", source = "git:https://github.com/acme/renox-acme#v0.4.1", isolation = "isolate" }
```

The key is the module's name and must equal the manifest's `[module].name` (MF3).

**`[authz]` and `[realtime]` of the app (1.1).** `renox.toml` may carry the same `[authz]` (`actions`, `sensitive`, `[authz.ownership]`, `[authz.entities]`, `[authz.default_roles]`) and `[realtime.feeds]` tables as a module manifest, for the app's own `app__*` tables and resources (`App::<Type>` in Cedar); the CLI resolves them into the artifact's `authz` and `realtime` blocks (`artifact.md` 1.3) and `renox check` applies MF13 and MF14 to them with the prefix `app__`. The app's policies are `policies/*.cedar` in the app root, built into `policies/app/`, with the schema `policies/schema.cedarschema`.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | range (section 2) | yes | The versions the tenant accepts. The lock's version must satisfy it and every dependant's range (MF2) |
| `source` | `path:<dir>` \| `git:https://<repo>#<ref>` | no | Where the module tree is. `path:` is relative to the app root (`..` allowed, no absolute path, no drive letter); `git:` names a tag or a commit, which the lock pins to a 40-hex commit. **Absent = an official module**, resolved by the CLI from the official module set of its own release (Open 1). 1.2: `registry:<publisher>/<name>` resolves from the Renox module registry (section 5, "Registry modules"); `<name>` is the module's name (MF3). `docs/10-modules.md` writes `registry = "acme/reports"`; the contract spells it as a `source` value so one key names where a module comes from |
| `mount` | `/` or `/<segment>(/<segment>)*`, static segments | no, default `/<name>` | The path prefix of the module's routes (`artifact.md` section 3, "Modules"). Collisions after mounting are rejected at build (`artifact.md` V21) |
| `config` | key → string, integer, or boolean | no | Values for the module's `[config]` keys. Unknown keys, wrong types, values outside bounds, and missing required keys are rejected (MF10) |
| `isolation` | `"shared"` \| `"isolate"` | no, default: the manifest's | Overrides the mode **downward only**: from `shared` to `isolate`. Asking for `shared` when the manifest says `isolate` is rejected (MF11) |
| `app_tables` (1.3) | array of `app__<table>` names, at most 64 | no, default none | The app's tables this module may use at its `permissions.app_access` (section 2). Each is an `app__` table; a module's or the platform's table is rejected; a grant to a module that asks no `app_access` is rejected (MF16). Changing the list needs `renox approve <module>` like any permission change |

## 5. `renox.lock`

```toml
version = 1

[[module]]
name = "auth"
version = "1.0.0"
source = "path:modules/auth"
hash = "<64 hex>"
isolation = "shared"
mount = "/auth"
dependencies = []
config = { registration = "open", session_days = 30, magic_links = true }
approved = { tables = "auth__*", network = ["accounts.google.com"], secrets = ["AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"], slots = [], hooks = [], roles = ["admin", "member"] }

[[module]]                                       # 1.2: a registry module
name = "tax_gcc"
version = "2.1.0"
source = "registry:gulfsoft/tax_gcc"
hash = "<64 hex>"
key_id = "ed25519:<43 base64url>"
signature = "<86 base64url>"
approved_version = "2.0.0"
isolation = "isolate"
mount = "/tax"
dependencies = []
config = {}
approved = { tables = "tax_gcc__*", network = [], secrets = [], slots = [], hooks = [] }
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | `1`, this contract's lock format |
| `module[]` | One entry per installed module, in **topological order**: every module after all its dependencies, ties by name. This is the migration order and the artifact's `modules` order (`artifact.md` section 3) |
| `name`, `version` | The manifest's name and version (MF3, MF12) |
| `source` | `official`, `path:<dir>` (as in `renox.toml`), `git:https://<repo>#<40-hex commit>`, or (1.2) `registry:<publisher>/<name>` |
| `hash` | SHA-256 of the module tree: the canonical listing of `artifact.md` section 2 over every regular file under the module directory, `module.toml` included. Reproducible with the `sha256sum` pipeline there. A `path:` module whose tree changed fails MF12 until `renox install` updates the lock |
| `isolation` | The effective mode after the `renox.toml` override (MF11) |
| `mount` | The effective mount (`renox.toml` or the default) |
| `dependencies` | The names of the manifest's `[dependencies]`, sorted: the dependency edges (MF12) |
| `config` | The resolved config: every declared key that has a value, from `renox.toml` or the default (MF12) |
| `approved` | The permissions the tenant approved: `tables` (absent when none), `network`, `secrets`, `slots`, `hooks`, from 1.1 `roles` (absent or empty when the module assigns no role; section 3), and from 1.3 `app_access` (the manifest's, absent when none) and `app_tables` (the `renox.toml` grant, sorted; absent or empty when none) |
| `key_id`, `signature` | 1.2, registry sources only (MF15): the publisher key and the `module.sig` signature the CLI verified at install. Absent for every other source |
| `approved_version` | 1.2, optional: the module version `approved` was given for. Absent = `version`. After `renox install` upgrades a module whose permissions did not change, the approval carries over and this keeps the older version; when they changed, MF12 fails until `renox approve`, which shows the diff from the `approved_version` set and then sets `approved_version = version` |

### Registry modules (1.2)

- **Publishing.** `renox publish` (run in a module tree with `[publisher]`) computes the module tree hash (above), signs it, writes `module.sig`, and uploads the tree to the registry under `<publisher>/<name>@<version>`. A version, once published, is immutable; the registry refuses a second upload of the same version.
- **`module.sig`** is a JSON object (`module-manifest.schema.json` `$defs/moduleSig`): `{ "version": 1, "publisher", "key_id", "name", "module_version", "hash", "signature" }`. `signature` is the Ed25519 signature (base64url, no padding) of the UTF-8 bytes `renox-module-v1\n<publisher>/<name>@<module_version>\n<hash>\n`. The tree hash is computed **without** `module.sig`, so the signature does not sign itself.
- **Installing.** `renox add` and `renox install` download the tree, recompute the hash, check `module.sig` against the publisher's key from the registry (refusing a revoked key), check that `[publisher].name` and `[module].name` match the source, and then show the permissions for approval as for any source (section 3). The lock records `key_id` and `signature`; `renox check` re-verifies the signature over the locked hash offline (MF15).
- **Upgrades.** A registry upgrade with changed `[permissions]` shows the diff against the approved set (`approved_version`) and needs `renox approve` (section 3, MF12); `docs/23-failure-modes.md`, "Marketplace module asks for new permissions".

The lock is the input to the build: `renox build` resolves nothing; it reads the lock, checks it (MF1–MF12), and copies it into the artifact. `renox install` resolves (newest version satisfying every range) and rewrites the lock; `renox approve` rewrites `approved`.

## 6. Rules

Applied by `renox check`, `renox build`, and `renox install` (P11, #235). `validate.ts` implements them for the examples. "Single file" rules need only one document; "project" rules need `renox.toml`, `renox.lock`, and the module trees together.

| # | Rule | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MF1 | **Names.** A module name matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, contains no `__`, does not end with `_`, and is not `app`, `renox`, or (1.1) `authz`, the namespace of the platform event `authz.roles_changed` (`ops.md` section 17). This applies to `[module].name`, `[dependencies]` keys, `renox.toml [modules]` keys, and lock names. With this rule, no module's prefix `<a>__` is a prefix of another's tables: `a__x` cannot belong to a module `a_`, since `a_` is not a name (the authorizer's rule, `crates/renox-data/src/authorizer.rs`) | single file |
| MF2 | **Versions.** Every `version` is semver and every range is of section 2. The lock's version of each module satisfies its `renox.toml` range and the range of every installed module that depends on it | single file, project |
| MF3 | **One install per name and prefix.** The `renox.toml` key, the manifest's `[module].name`, and the lock entry's `name` are the same; no two installed modules (or a module and `app`) have the same name; no installed module's prefix is a prefix of another's; each `renox.toml` module has exactly one lock entry and the lock has no other | single file (lock), project |
| MF4 | **Own prefix only.** `permissions.tables`, when present, is exactly `"<name>__*"` (in the manifest and in the lock's `approved`); every secret name starts with `<NAME>_`, the module name in upper case | single file |
| MF5 | **Dependency graph.** Every `[dependencies]` entry is installed; a name in both `[dependencies]` and `[optional_dependencies]` is rejected (1.4); no module depends on itself; the graph has no cycle (rejected at build, not at call, `docs/10-modules.md` rule 1); the lock lists every module after its dependencies | single file (lock), project |
| MF6 | **Export names.** Views are `<name>__public_<id>_v<n>` with this module's name; events and hook points start with `<name>.`; payload, argument, and result schemas use only the keyword subset of `validate.ts` | single file |
| MF7 | **Imports.** Every `[imports]` service `<dep>.<service>` and view `<dep>__public_…` names a module in `[dependencies]` whose installed manifest exports it | project |
| MF8 | **Fills.** `permissions.slots` is exactly the set of `[[slots]].name`; every hook in `permissions.hooks` is exported by an installed module other than this one, except a hook `<dep>.*` where `<dep>` is in `[optional_dependencies]` and not installed (1.4) | single file, project |
| MF9 | **References.** Every `[[slots]].template` exists in the module tree; every `[[slots]].requires` and `[[tools]].action` is in `[authz].actions` | single file, project |
| MF10 | **Config.** A declaration's `default` has its `type` and passes `values`, `min`, `max`, `max_length`; `min ≤ max`; `required = true` has no `default`. Every `renox.toml` config key is declared; every value has the declared type and passes its bounds; every required key has a value | single file, project |
| MF11 | **Sources and isolation.** `source` is `path:`, `git:`, or (1.2) `registry:`; a `renox.toml` `isolation` is never lower than the manifest's (`shared` below `isolate`); the lock's `isolation` is the effective one | project |
| MF12 | **Lock matches.** For each module: the lock's `version` is the manifest's; `hash` is the hash of the module tree; `dependencies` are the manifest's; `config` is the resolved config; `mount` and `source` are the `renox.toml` values (or the defaults); **`approved` equals the manifest's `[permissions]`** (section 3), `roles` included from 1.1 and `app_access` from 1.3 | project |
| MF13 | **Actions and roles** (1.1). `permissions.roles` is exactly the set of `[authz.default_roles]` keys; every action of a `default_roles` entry, every `sensitive` action, every `slots[].requires`, and every `tools[].action` is in `[authz].actions` (MF9 for the last two); for the app's `renox.toml [authz]`, the same with the merged action set | single file |
| MF14 | **Own prefix** (1.1). Every `[authz.ownership]` table, every `[authz.entities].table`, and every `[realtime.feeds]` table starts with `<name>__` (`app__` in `renox.toml`); every `[[tools]].file` exists in the module tree | single file, project (the file) |
| MF15 | **Registry signatures** (1.2). A lock entry has `key_id` and `signature` exactly when its `source` is `registry:`; the source's `<name>` is the entry's `name`; the manifest of a registry module has `[publisher]` with the source's publisher and the lock's `key_id`; the signature verifies over the locked hash (section 5, "Registry modules") | single file (lock); the publisher and signature checks run in the CLI at install and in `renox check` (they need the registry tree and key) |
| MF16 | **App tables** (1.3). Every `renox.toml` `app_tables` entry and every lock `approved.app_tables` entry starts with `app__`; the lock's `app_tables` is sorted and, when not empty, has `app_access`; the lock's `app_tables` is the `renox.toml` grant; a module granted `app_tables` asks for `permissions.app_access` | single file, project |

Every rejection names the rule (`MF1`–`MF16`), the file and key, and a one-line reason, and never a filesystem path outside the app.

## 7. What the other F4 contracts take from here

| Consumer | Takes | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Artifact 1.1 (#227) | The lock entries, in order, plus each module's `exports` and `[[slots]]` | `artifact.md` section 3, "Modules" |
| Ops 1.3.0 (#226) | Per-module `ctx` from `approved` and `config`; dependency checks from `dependencies`; export checks from `exports` | `ops.md` 1.3.0 (#226, not merged yet) |
| SDK (#236) | `[exports.services]` and the services' signatures | `renox-modules.d.ts` |
| Migrations (#234) | Lock order as migration order; `permissions.tables` for which modules must have migrations | `artifact.md` V19 |
| Artifact 1.3 and ops 1.5.0 (#272, F5) | `[authz]`, `[realtime]`, `[[tools]]` on the module entry and as `tool` routes; `approved.roles` for `op_authz_roles_*`; the `auth.principal` service and hook for the principal | `artifact.md` section 3, "Authorization and realtime"; `ops.md` sections 17–19 |
| Artifact 1.4 and ops 1.7.0 (#318, F7) | `[storage]` on the module entry; `isolation = "isolate"` run by #320; `registry:` sources in the entry's `source` | `artifact.md` section 3, "Storage, AI, and the SBOM"; `ops.md` sections 15.6, 21 |
| Ops 1.8.0 (#346, F7) | `approved.app_access` and `approved.app_tables`, copied with `approved` into the artifact (`artifact.md` V22), for the authorizer's app-table rule and its audit | `ops.md` section 1, "App tables" |

## 8. Examples

[`examples/manifest/`](examples/manifest/):

- `module.<case>.(valid|invalid).toml`: single manifests. The valid ones include the manifests of the F4 catalog modules in `docs/18-build-plan.md`: `auth` (M1), `org` (M2), `gcc` (M23, catalog name `gcc-data`), and `i18n` (M12 with the M19 core), plus the `billing` manifest of `docs/10-modules.md`, which carries the 1.1 `[authz]`, `[realtime]`, `[[tools]]`, and `permissions.roles` (section 2).
- `renox.<case>.(valid|invalid).toml` and `renox-lock.<case>.(valid|invalid).toml`: single `renox.toml` and lock files.
- `projects/<case>.(valid|invalid)/`: a whole app (`renox.toml`, `renox.lock`, `modules/<name>/…`) for the project rules. `projects/shop.valid` installs `auth`, `org`, `gcc`, and `i18n` from `path:` sources; `projects/app-tables.valid` grants a module an app table (1.3).

An invalid file names its reason as `[expect: <reason>]` in a TOML comment (for a project, in its `renox.toml`), and `validate.ts` checks that it fails for that reason.

## 9. Versioning

- The lock carries `version = 1`. A CLI refuses a lock with a version it does not know.
- **Minor** (no version bump): a new optional key with a default that keeps old behaviour, a new range form, a new rule that only rejects what was already meaningless.
- **Major**: renaming or removing a key, changing a default, changing the hash rule. Lands with the CLI and the broker in one PR.
- Contract edits are made only by `type:contract` issues.

## Open

1. **Official module distribution.** A `renox.toml` entry without `source` is an official module "from the CLI's release". Whether the CLI embeds `modules/*` or downloads them from the release assets (signed like the worker, #129) is decided by #235; the lock records `source = "official"` either way, and the hash pins the tree.
2. **`isolate` mode.** Settled in 1.2: the runtime semantics are `ops.md` 1.7.0 section 15.6, implemented by #320. Until #320 lands, #235's build error for `isolate` stays.
3. **Registry sources.** Settled in 1.2 (sections 2, 4, 5; MF15). Still open: the registry's own HTTP API (publish, fetch, key listing and revocation) belongs to the registry service of #329 and is not a tenant-facing contract here; payouts for `price` are an owner decision (`docs/15`).
4. **Slot exports.** A slot is filled by name; nothing declares which module renders `<r-slot name="admin.sidebar">`. A filled slot that nothing renders is harmless (it never appears). An `[exports].slots` list can be added as a minor change if `renox check` needs to warn about it.
5. **App events.** The app has no manifest, so it cannot export events or hook points in F4. `renox.toml [exports]` can be added as a minor change.
6. **App-table grants by column or row (1.3).** `app_tables` grants a whole table. A column list (hide `app__customers.email` from a reports module) or a row filter would need the authorizer's column callback and a rewrite the authorizer cannot do; left out until a module needs it. The app can expose a view `app__<x>` with the columns it chooses and grant that instead.
7. **Dashboard approval of app-table grants (1.3).** The grant is in `renox.toml`, so it reaches the control plane only through an artifact. Whether the dashboard shows "module X can write app__orders" before activation, like a permission diff, is #335's to decide.

---

Source: modules/2fa/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/2fa/README.md)

# 2fa

Two-step verification (`docs/18-build-plan.md` M3; `docs/24-threat-model.md`, "Account takeover"). After the password, or a magic link, OAuth, phone or passkey sign-in, a user who has a second factor confirms it before any session starts. The factor can be an authenticator app (TOTP), a passkey, or a recovery code. The principal then carries `mfa_verified`, so a policy can require it.

The module is named `twofa`, because a module name cannot start with a digit (`manifest.md` MF1). Its tables are `twofa__*` and it is usually mounted at `/2fa`.

## Install

```toml
[modules]
twofa = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/2fa", config = { step_up_minutes = 15 } }
```

```
renox secrets set TWOFA_KEY <32 random bytes, base64>
```

`renox add twofa` asks to approve:

- the hooks `auth.after_login` and `auth.principal`;
- the slot `account.sections`;
- the secret `TWOFA_KEY`, which seals the TOTP secrets and the pending sign-ins.

| Config | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `step_up_minutes` | 15 | How long a verification counts, for `mfa_verified` and for `requireRecent` |
| `allow_totp` | `true` | Authenticator apps |
| `allow_passkeys` | `true` | Passkeys as a second factor |
| `recovery_codes` | 10 | Codes per set (4 to 20) |
| `issuer` | `""` | The name authenticator apps show; empty = the host |
| `base_path` | `/2fa` | The mount, for links and redirects |
| `passkey_rp_id`, `passkey_origin` | `""` | The WebAuthn relying party; empty = the request's host |

## Flows

1. **Enrol.** `/2fa/enroll/totp` shows a QR code, drawn as an inline SVG by `lib/qr.ts`, and the key as text. The first code turns TOTP on and shows the recovery codes once. `/2fa/enroll/passkey` registers a passkey. Enrolling counts as a verification of the current session.
2. **Sign in.** auth runs `auth.after_login` with a single-use `resume` ticket.
   - If the user has a factor, this module keeps the ticket, sealed, under a 10-minute `__Host-renox_2fa` cookie, and answers a 303 to `/2fa/verify?next=`. No session exists yet.
   - A correct TOTP code, passkey or recovery code redeems the ticket through `auth.resumeLogin`, which starts the session and emits `auth.login`.
   - The session is recorded as verified (`twofa__sessions`).
3. **Step up.** For a signed-in user, `/2fa/verify` refreshes the session's verification. Removing a factor and making new recovery codes need a recent one.

The rules on codes and attempts:

- A TOTP code works once. A code of the last accepted 30-second step, or an earlier one, is refused (RFC 6238 section 5.2).
- A recovery code works once and is stored as a SHA-256.
- A pending sign-in allows 5 failures, then ends.
- A user gets 10 failures in 15 minutes.

## The principal and policies

The `auth.principal` filler sets `mfa_verified`. It is true while this session's verification is younger than `step_up_minutes`. A policy that needs it:

```cedar
permit (principal is Renox::User, action == Renox::Action::"invoice.refund", resource)
when { principal has mfa_verified && principal.mfa_verified };
```

The cell caches the principal for up to 60 s. A new sign-in, a logout or a role change drops the cache at once. A step-up within an existing session, or the window running out, shows in the principal within that time. An action that must be sure calls `requireRecent`, which reads the table:

```ts
import { twofa } from "renox:modules";

export const actions = {
  async refund(ctx) {
    await twofa.requireRecent({ within: 5, next: ctx.url.pathname }); // throws STEP_UP_REQUIRED with details.verify_url
    // ...
  },
};
```

## Services

| Service | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `isEnrolled(userId)` | Whether the user has TOTP or a passkey |
| `requireRecent({ within?, next? })` | Resolves when this session verified within `within` minutes (default `step_up_minutes`). Otherwise it throws `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` (status 403), with `details.verify_url` |
| `verifiedAt(sessionId)` | Unix ms of the session's last verification, or `null` |

## The account page

`partials/account.html` fills auth's slot `account.sections` with a link to `/2fa`. A slot keeps auth free of any knowledge of 2fa, and the link only needs the mount. The rest of the management is on `/2fa`.

## Passkeys here and in auth

A passkey in auth (#291) is a way to sign in without a password. A passkey here is a second factor after one. They are separate tables (`auth__passkeys`, `twofa__webauthn`), so a user may have both.

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/twofa.test.ts` against `tests/app`. That app has i18n, auth and twofa, a refund action that needs `mfa_verified`, and `TWOFA_KEY` in `.env.test`. The tests cover:

- enrolment;
- the halted sign-in and its resumption;
- a replayed TOTP code;
- a recovery code used twice;
- passkeys with the recorded vectors;
- `mfa_verified` and the refund, before and after;
- step-up expiry;
- the verify rate limit;
- English and Arabic snapshots;
- no secret, key or code in logs or snapshots.

The QR encoder was checked module for module against python-qrcode, for versions 1 to 15 and all eight masks. The policy cases are in `policies/tests/2fa.json`.

Source: modules/admin/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/admin/README.md)

# admin (#335)

The app's back office. It provides:
- a layout with the `admin.sidebar` slot;
- a dashboard with the `admin.dashboard` slot, which the installed modules fill;
- the users page, where the admin role is granted and revoked;
- the audit viewer.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add admin          # needs auth, i18n and audit
```

```toml
admin = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/admin", config = { title = "Back office" } }
```

The app grants the first admin with `ctx.authz.roles.assign(user_id, "admin")` from its own code, for example a one-off setup route. After that, admins grant each other from the users page.

## Pages

| Page | Needs | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mount>` | `admin.access` | The user count, the latest audit events (with `audit.read`), and the cards of `admin.dashboard` |
| `<mount>/users?q=` | `admin.access` | The users from auth's public view and whether each holds the admin role |
| Grant and revoke buttons on the users page | `admin.users` (sensitive) | Shown under `r-can`. An admin cannot revoke their own role |
| `<mount>/audit?actor=&action=` | `admin.access` | The audit module's trail. It also needs `audit.read`, the auditor role; without it the page says so and shows no rows |

The default policy grants both admin actions to the `admin` role.

## Slots other modules fill

| Module | `admin.sidebar` link | Shown when the user holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| billing | All invoices | `billing.manage` |
| storage | Files | `storage.manage` |
| jobs | Jobs | `jobs.read` |
| notifications | Notification preferences | (everyone) |

A filler renders only when its module is installed and the user holds its `requires` action.

## Not built

- **CRUD scaffolding from `[admin.tables]`.** A module may read and write only its own `<name>__*` tables (the authorizer, `ops.md` section 3), so a back office module cannot edit the app's `app__*` tables. Scaffolding needs a contract change: either an app-granted table permission for one module, or a scaffold that `renox` generates into the app's own pages.
- **The organisations page.**
- **Settings beyond `admin__settings`.**

## Tests

With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app with auth, audit and jobs on the worker:
- the back office is refused without `admin.access`;
- the sidebar renders jobs' link and not billing's, which is not installed;
- the admin role is granted and revoked, but not an admin's own;
- the audit viewer is refused without the auditor role and shows the role decisions to an auditor;
- the users table header is snapshotted in `ltr` and `rtl`.

Source: modules/audit/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/audit/README.md)

# audit

An append-only audit trail for an app and its modules (`docs/18-build-plan.md` M8; `docs/11-authorization.md` "Cross-module context and audit"). Modules and the app record events through one service. Nothing can edit or delete them. The platform's authorization decisions on sensitive actions appear in the same trail.

## Install

```toml
[modules]
audit = { version = "^1.0", config = { retain_days = 365 } }
```

A module that records events adds `audit = "^1.0"` to its `[dependencies]` and `services = ["audit.record"]` to its `[imports]`. Depending on `audit` also lets that module read the platform view `renox__authz_audit_v1` directly.

## The event

`audit__events`, one row per event:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Random, sortable by time |
| `at` | Unix ms (as in `renox__authz_audit`) |
| `actor_kind` | `user`, `agent` or `system` |
| `actor_id` | The user id (the agent's user for `agent`), or `system:<module>` |
| `client` | The agent's client name (`agent` only) |
| `action` | `<module>.<verb>`, such as `invoice.refund` or `auth.login` |
| `resource_type`, `resource_id` | What was acted on (`billing:Invoice`, `inv_1`), optional |
| `result` | `ok`, `denied` or `failed` |
| `details` | A JSON object, redacted (below), at most 16 KB |
| `request_id` | Optional, to tie a row to logs |
| `source` | `record`, or the name of the event a listener recorded |

### Actor kinds

- `user`: a person, acting in a browser.
- `agent`: a person's agent through the app's `/mcp`, with the agent's client name in `client`. It can do only what its user can (`docs/20-ai-agents-mcp.md` section 5, "Attribution").
- `system`: the platform or a module acting on its own (an event handler, a job), as `system:<module>`.

### Redaction

The redaction rule applies to `details` at any depth. Each key is split into words (`apiKey`, `api_key` and `API-KEY` all become `api key`). The key's value becomes `"[redacted]"` when either:

- one of the words is `password`, `pass`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `credential`, `otp`, `pin`, `cvv`, `iban`, `signature`, `salt`, `hash` (and a few spellings of these); or
- the words run together into `apikey`, `privatekey`, `accesskey`, `cardnumber`, `sessionid` or `clientsecret`.

Values are never inspected, so a secret stored under an innocent key stays: name keys for what they hold.

## Services

| Service | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `record(event)` | `{ id }`. `event` is `{ action, actor: { kind, id, client? }, resource?: { type, id? }, result?, details?, request_id? }`. A malformed event throws |
| `query(filter?)` | `{ events, next }`, newest first. The events are this module's rows merged with the platform's decisions from `renox__authz_audit_v1` (`kind: "authz"`, `result` `allow`/`deny`). Filter: `actor`, `action` (or a prefix ending in `.`), `since`, `until`, `platform` (default `true`), `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `cursor` (the previous page's `next`). Requires `audit.read` |
| `exportEvents(filter?, purpose?)` | Runs the hook `audit.export` once per page of 200 (`{ events, page, last, purpose }`); returns `{ events, pages }`. For F7's reports and the F6 erasure task (#120). Requires `audit.read` |
| `prune()` | Deletes rows older than `retain_days`, never fewer than 30 days; returns `{ deleted }`. The module's job `jobs/prune.ts` runs it every night at 02:30 UTC (#297), so the app no longer has to; the app may still call it |

## Who may read

`audit.read` is the module's action, and it is `sensitive`: every read, allowed or denied, writes its own row in `renox__authz_audit`. `policies/audit.cedar` allows it to the role `auditor`. The app grants that role (`ctx.authz.roles.assign(userId, "auditor")`); the module never grants it.

## Listeners

These events become rows with no code in the app (`hooks.ts`, `on`):

| Event | Actor |
| --- | --- |
| `auth.login`, `auth.password_changed`, `auth.agent_token_revoked` | The user |
| `authz.roles_changed` | `system:authz`; `details` names the user, the role and `op` |
| `org.created`, `org.member_added` | The user |
| `org.member_removed` | `by`, the user who removed the member |

## Append-only

- **Updates are refused.** `audit__events` has triggers that `RAISE(ABORT)` on every `UPDATE`.
- **Young rows cannot be deleted.** The same triggers refuse a `DELETE` of any row younger than 30 days.
- **This covers every connection.** It holds for the module's own code, other modules, the app, and a tool that opens the file.
- **Other modules cannot write the table at all.** The SQLite authorizer refuses them `audit__*`.
- **The platform table is the authorizer's job.** `renox__authz_audit` (#277) is refused `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `DROP` and `ALTER` for everyone.

The manifest has no `append_only` permission (#272 did not add one), so the triggers are the module's rule. To make them possible, the migration runner lets a module create triggers on its own tables. Their bodies may only `select raise(...)`, with no subquery.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retain_days` | 365 | `prune` deletes rows older than this, from 30 to 3650 days |

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/audit.test.ts` against `tests/app`. That app has auth, org, audit, and the fixture `tamper`: a module that depends on audit, tries to edit its rows, and fills `audit.export`. The tests cover:

- the redaction rule;
- the listeners;
- `record` from another module;
- append-only, against module code, app code and the file itself (the `docs/24-threat-model.md` row "Audit library append-only; tenant cannot edit or delete audit rows");
- `query` refused without the role and allowed with it, with the platform decisions joined and paged;
- export;
- prune.

The policy cases are in `policies/tests/audit.json`.

---

Source: modules/auth/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/auth/README.md)

# auth

Users, passwords, sessions, and the sign-in pages for a Renox app, as a module (`docs/10-modules.md`; M1 of `docs/18-build-plan.md`). An app that installs it has accounts with no auth code of its own: `examples/shop` is the reference (#241).

## Install

```sh
renox add i18n          # auth's pages take their locale from i18n (#244)
renox add auth          # shows the tables, hosts, secrets and slot it asks for; approve with y
renox migrate           # creates auth__* (renox dev does it on start)
```

`renox.toml`:

```toml
[modules]
auth = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/auth", config = { session_idle_hours = 24 } }
```

The pages are under the mount: `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`, `/auth/account`, `/auth/magic`, `/auth/reset`, and the OAuth routes `/auth/oauth/<provider>/{start,callback}`.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session_idle_hours` | 24 | A session ends after this many hours without a request |
| `session_absolute_days` | 30 | A session ends this many days after sign-in, used or not; the cookie's `Max-Age` |
| `password_min_length` | 12 | At register, password change, and reset |
| `login_path` | `/auth/login` | Where `requireUser` and `loginUrl` send a signed-out visitor; change it with the mount |
| `google_client_id`, `github_client_id`, `microsoft_client_id` | `""` | OAuth client ids; a provider is on when its id and its secret are set |

## Permissions

| What | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tables | `auth__*` | users, sessions, identities, tokens, attempts |
| Network | `accounts.google.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, `www.googleapis.com`, `github.com`, `api.github.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `graph.microsoft.com` | OAuth token endpoints, OIDC signing keys, the GitHub API; nothing else |
| Secrets | `AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | Only for the providers you set up |
| Slots | `app.header` | The user menu |

Other modules read users through the view `auth__public_users_v1` (`id`, `email`, `display_name`, `created_at`), never the tables: the authorizer refuses `auth__users` to them.

## Services

Through `import { auth } from "renox:modules"` (or `ctx.services.auth`):

| Service | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `currentUser()` | The signed-in user of this request, or `null` |
| `currentSession()` | `{ id, user }` of the live session, or `null`. `id` is not the cookie token: other modules key per-session state by it (org's active organisation) |
| `requireUser()` | The user, or throws `AuthRequiredError` (`code: "AUTH_REQUIRED"`, `status: 401`; through the broker, `RENOX_MODULE_SERVICE`) |
| `loginUrl(next?)` | `/auth/login?next=…`; `next` kept only when it is a path of the app |
| `register({ email, password, display_name? })` | `{ message }` (a confirmation link is mailed; the same message when the email already has an account, which gets a mail saying so) or `{ error }` for a bad email or password |
| `login({ email, password })` | `{ user, cookie }` or `{ error }`: the same error for an unknown email, a wrong password, and a locked account |
| `logout()` | `{ cookie }` (clears it); the session is revoked server side |
| `sendMagicLink({ email })`, `requestPasswordReset({ email })` | `{ message }`: the same in every case |
| `confirmPasswordReset({ token, password })` | `{ cookie }` or `{ error }` |
| `principal(sessionId)` | `{ id, attrs }` of the signed-in user, or `null` (below, "The principal") |
| `resumeLogin(ticket)` | `{ cookie, session_id, user_id, next }` for a `resume` ticket of `auth.after_login`, or `null` (unknown, used, or past 10 minutes). Starts the session; the hook does not run again |
| `verifyAgentToken(token)` | `{ principal, scopes, client: { name } }` for a live agent token, or `null`. The cell calls it for `/mcp` |
| `oauthMetadata(issuer)` | The RFC 8414 document the cell serves at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server<mount>/oauth` |
| `listAgentTokens()`, `revokeAgentToken(id)` | The signed-in user's connected agents; revoke one of them |

A page that needs a user:

```ts
import { auth } from "renox:modules";
import { redirect } from "@renoxium/sdk";

export async function load(ctx) {
  const user = await auth.currentUser();
  if (user === null) return redirect.safe(await auth.loginUrl(ctx.url.pathname));
  return { auth_user: user };
}
```

## Events

| Event | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `auth.user_registered` | `{ user_id, at, source: "password" \| "oauth" }` |
| `auth.login` | `{ user_id, at }` |
| `auth.password_changed` | `{ user_id, at }` (a reset) |
| `auth.logout` | `{ user_id, at }`: the cell drops the principal from its cache |
| `auth.agent_token_revoked` | `{ token_hash, user_id, at }`: the cell drops the token from its `/mcp` cache |

All durable: written in the transaction of the request, delivered after it commits.

## Hooks

| Hook | When | A filler may |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.before_register` | Before a user is created (`{ email, display_name }`) | Halt with its own response: invite-only, a domain allowlist |
| `auth.after_login` | After the password, magic link, OAuth, phone or passkey check, before any session starts (`{ user_id, next?, resume }`) | Halt with its own response, so no session starts. To resume later, keep `resume` (a single-use ticket, valid 10 minutes) and call `auth.resumeLogin(resume)`, which starts the session. 2fa does this |
| `auth.principal` | Once per request, while the cell resolves the principal (`{ principal: { id, attrs } }`) | Extend `principal.attrs` in place: 2fa sets `mfa_verified`, org sets `org`. Keys outside the platform's user attributes are dropped |
| `auth.send_otp` | A one-time code must reach a phone (`{ to, code, purpose: "login" \| "verify" }`) | Deliver it. whatsapp fills it (#290); an SMS module will in F7. Never log the code |
| `auth.send_sms` | Declared for F7 (`{ to, text }`) | Nothing fills it yet |
| `auth.agent_audit` | An agent was connected or disconnected (`{ action: "connect" \| "revoke", user_id, client_name, scopes, at }`) | Write an audit row (the `audit` library, #288). Never carries the token |
| `auth.send_mail` | A mail must go out (`{ to, template: "magic_link" \| "password_reset" \| "verify_email" \| "account_exists", args: { url, expires_minutes, display_name } }`) | Send it. auth sends no mail itself until the email module (F7). Fill it from a small module of the app (`modules/mailer`, `permissions.hooks = ["auth.send_mail"]`) |

## Slots

`partials/user-menu.html` fills `app.header` when the app's layout has `<r-slot name="app.header" />`. It shows `auth_user.display_name` with a link to the account page, or "Sign in". A page puts `auth_user: await auth.currentUser()` in its data.

## Overrides

Override a template, never the code: put a copy at `overrides/auth/pages/login.html` (or any `pages/` or `partials/` file) in the app. `renox build` compiles it in place of the original and records the original's hash in the app's `overrides.json`. After `renox add auth` brings a new version whose original changed, `renox build` and `renox check` warn with a diff (`--strict` fails). Update the override, then delete its entry from `overrides.json`.

## Sessions and cookies

- `__Host-renox_auth=<32 random bytes, hex>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=<absolute expiry>`. Only the token's SHA-256 is stored.
- A new session at every sign-in; the browser's previous one is revoked (fixation). A password change revokes every other session and rotates this one.
- This is not the platform's page `session.id` (`ops.md` section 14). That one exists before sign-in, lives as long as the browser keeps it, and carries the CSRF token. A user session has its own lifetime and ends at logout.
- Passwords are argon2id at m = 64 MiB, t = 3, p = 1 through `ctx.password` (a platform op, off the isolate thread). An unknown email is checked against a fixed hash, so it costs the same.
- Failure buckets: 10 per account and 30 per IP address per 15 minutes; past either, the same generic message. Magic and reset links: 5 per email per 15 minutes, single use, 15 minutes, bound to the user agent family that asked.
- OAuth: `state` in a 10-minute `__Host-renox_oauth` cookie, compared in constant time; PKCE S256 for Google and Microsoft; ID tokens verified (RS256 against the provider's keys, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce). An existing account is linked only when the provider verified the email.

## The principal

The cell asks `auth.principal` once per request, before any guard (`ops.md` 1.5.0 section 17). Signed out, the answer is `null`, the anonymous principal. Signed in, it is:

```json
{ "id": "<user id>", "attrs": { "email_verified": true, "phone_verified": false, "created_at": 1793310868, "org": "o_1", "mfa_verified": true } }
```

- `email_verified`, `phone_verified` and `created_at` come from auth itself.
- Fillers of the hook `auth.principal` add the rest: `org` from org, `mfa_verified` from 2fa (#287). Only the platform's user attributes are kept (`created_at`, `email_verified`, `mfa_verified`, `org`, `phone_verified`).
- The cell adds the user's role assignments as `roles`.
- The cell caches the principal and drops it on `auth.login`, `auth.logout` and `authz.roles_changed`.
- Code reads it as `ctx.principal`; policies read it as `principal`.

## Sign-in methods

The login page offers the password form and, each behind its own switch:

- a link to phone sign-in (config `phone_login`);
- a link to passkey sign-in (config `passkeys`);
- a button per OAuth provider that has a client id and a secret: Google, GitHub, Microsoft, UAE PASS.

The `2fa` module (#287) fills both `auth.after_login` and `auth.principal`. After any of these methods, it halts the sign-in until the second factor. It keeps the `resume` ticket auth hands to `auth.after_login` fillers and redeems it with `resumeLogin` once the factor passed. It also sets `mfa_verified` on the principal.

Every method ends the same way as the password flow. The hook `auth.after_login` runs first; a filler may halt, and then no session starts (2fa). After it come a new session, `auth.login`, and a 303 to `next`.

### Phone (`phone_login = true`)

- **Pages.** `<mount>/phone` asks for the number and sends a code; `<mount>/phone/verify` takes the code. The account page adds or changes the phone with a code to the new number. A phone signs in only once it is verified.
- **Numbers.** UAE numbers are accepted as `+971 5x xxx xxxx`, `05x xxx xxxx` or `00971…`; numbers in any other E.164 form are accepted too.
- **Codes.** A code is 6 digits, lasts 5 minutes, allows 5 attempts and works once. It is stored as argon2id.
- **Same answer.** The sign-in request answers the same whether or not a user has the number, and sends nothing for an unknown one.
- **Buckets.** At most 5 codes per number and 30 per IP address in 15 minutes.
- **Delivery.** Codes go out through the hook `auth.send_otp`. Install `whatsapp` (#290), which fills it. auth cannot call an optional module, and a hook needs no dependency.

### Passkeys (`passkeys = true`)

- **Adding one.** `<mount>/passkeys/register` (linked from the account page) creates a discoverable credential, ES256 or RS256.
- **Signing in.** `<mount>/passkeys/login` signs in with it, without a username.
- **Verification.** Done with the SDK's `verifyRegistration` and `verifyAssertion`. Challenges are single use and last 5 minutes. The signature counter must grow, so a cloned authenticator is refused.
- **Relying party.** It is the request's host, or config `passkey_rp_id` and `passkey_origin`.
- **Not a second factor.** A passkey here is a way to sign in. A passkey as a second factor is the 2fa module's (#287), in its own table: a user may have either, or both.

### UAE PASS

UAE PASS is an OAuth 2 provider with the user-info endpoint. It is set up with config `uaepass_client_id`, `uaepass_env` (`staging` by default, or `production`) and the secret `AUTH_UAEPASS_CLIENT_SECRET`.

- `uuid` becomes `auth__users.uaepass_uuid`.
- An SOP3 account, a verified identity, sets `verified_identity`.
- The email of SOP2 and SOP3 accounts counts as verified, so it may link an existing account. An SOP1 email does not.

**Production onboarding (owner steps):**

1. Apply for UAE PASS integration as a private-sector service provider through UAE PASS's partner onboarding. Provide the legal entity, the trade licence and the use case.
2. Sign the service provider agreement and complete the security questionnaire.
3. Receive staging credentials. Register `https://<host><mount>/oauth/uaepass/callback` as the redirect URI.
4. Test on staging (`uaepass_env = "staging"`) with UAE PASS staging test accounts. The integration review checks the button design guidelines and the login flow.
5. Request production credentials. Set `uaepass_client_id`, the secret, and `uaepass_env = "production"`.

The requirements for private providers are an open question in `docs/15-roadmap.md`. Check them with the UAE PASS team before you promise the method to a customer.

## Agents (App MCP)

auth is the OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app's `/mcp` (`docs/20-ai-agents-mcp.md` section 2). An agent connects as a user and can do only what the user can.

- Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` names `https://<host><mount>/oauth`. The cell serves its metadata (RFC 8414) from `oauthMetadata`.
- Registration: `POST <mount>/oauth/register` (RFC 7591). Public clients only (`token_endpoint_auth_method: "none"`). Redirect URIs must be `https`, or `http` on loopback.
- Authorization: `GET <mount>/oauth/authorize`. PKCE S256 is required. A signed-out user goes to the login page first.
- Consent: `<mount>/oauth/consent` lists the client, the user, where it returns, and each scope (`tools:*` or `tools:<name>`), with Allow and Deny. It runs no script of its own and cannot be framed.
- Codes: one minute, single use, stored hashed. A failed exchange also burns the code.
- Token: `POST <mount>/oauth/token` returns `renox_agt_<64 hex>`, valid one hour, with no refresh token. Only its SHA-256 is stored (`auth__agent_tokens`).
- Revoking: the account page's "Connected agents" lists each live token with its client, scopes and last use. "Disconnect" revokes one and emits `auth.agent_token_revoked`, and the cell refuses the token from then on.

Proof: `tests/oauth.test.ts`:

- the full flow;
- a wrong verifier and a reused code;
- a narrowed scope;
- deny;
- no PKCE and an unregistered redirect;
- revoke from the account page;
- a consent page that cannot be framed and sets no cookie.

These keep the `docs/24-threat-model.md` row "Account takeover of a tenant developer" whole: agent tokens are hashed, last one hour, are listed, and can be revoked.

## Policies

`policies/auth.cedar` (a user reads and updates only their own account and revokes only their own sessions) and `policies/tests/auth.json` hold the default policy and its cases. They are files only until the policy engine (F5); `renox test` lists the cases as pending.

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/*.test.ts` in `tests/app/`, with the fixture modules `reader`, `mailer` and `otpbox`. `otpbox` records codes in place of whatsapp, extends the principal, and halts `auth.after_login` for chosen users. The tests cover:

- register, login, logout, rotation, expiry, buckets, the public view, magic links, reset;
- OAuth with a fake provider, and UAE PASS with a fake IdP;
- the principal: its shape, filler attributes, roles, logout;
- phone sign-in;
- passkeys with recorded vectors;
- agents (OAuth 2.1 for `/mcp`);
- install and upgrade into the shop;
- per-role snapshots (`tests/__snapshots__/`).

## Security tests

`tests/negative/` (#100): one file per attack, with the `docs/24-threat-model.md` F4 and `docs/23-failure-modes.md` section 5 rows each one proves.

| File | Case | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session-fixation.test.ts` | A session token planted in the victim's browser before sign-in | A new token at sign-in; the planted one is revoked |
| `session-fixation.test.ts` | Password change | This session rotated, every other one signed out |
| `logout.test.ts` | A cookie copied before logout, replayed after | Refused (server-side revocation); "sign out everywhere" ends every session |
| `token-replay.test.ts` | Magic link used twice; from another browser family | Refused; tokens live 15 minutes and are stored hashed |
| `token-replay.test.ts` | Reset token reused, or past 15 minutes | Refused; the password stays |
| `oauth-state-pkce.test.ts` | Callback with a forged state, another flow's state, or no flow cookie | Refused before the code exchange, no session |
| `oauth-state-pkce.test.ts` | Code exchanged with another PKCE verifier | Refused by the provider (a fake Google in the test process) |
| `enumeration.test.ts` | Login, register, reset, magic link for an existing and a missing account | The same status and message, no cookie at register; timing within 20 % |
| `brute-force.test.ts` | 10 failures per account, 30 per IP in 15 minutes | Locked with the generic message, which is snapshotted with the register, reset and magic-link messages; unlocked in the next window |
| `password-hashing.test.ts` | The stored hash | argon2id v19, m = 65536, t = 3, p = 1, 16-byte salt, 32-byte digest, a different salt per user |
| `cookies.test.ts` | The session, logout and OAuth flow cookies | `__Host-`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` |

## Language

auth's pages ask `i18n.detectLocale` for the locale, passing the signed-in user, and set it. Their text comes from `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/ar.json`, keys `auth.*`. An app re-words a label with the same key in its own catalog. Messages computed in code (errors, notices) are English for now.

---

Source: modules/billing/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/billing/README.md)

# billing (#329)

Payments for an app's own customers:
- plans and subscriptions;
- one-off checkouts, one per order;
- invoices, refunds and metered usage;
- a PSP adapter, with Stripe UAE first and the GCC providers in #330;
- Stripe's webhooks, verified by the platform.

Amounts are integers in minor units (fils for AED). Card data never reaches the app: the customer pays on the provider's page.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add billing                                   # needs auth and i18n
bunx renox secrets set BILLING_STRIPE_KEY sk_live_…      # or sk_test_… while testing
bunx renox secrets set BILLING_WEBHOOK_STRIPE_SECRET whsec_…
```

```toml
billing = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/billing", config = { currency = "AED", success_url = "/orders", cancel_url = "/cart" } }
```

In the Stripe dashboard, point a webhook endpoint at `https://<app host>/billing/webhooks/stripe`. Send it these events:
- `checkout.session.completed`
- `invoice.finalized`
- `invoice.paid`
- `invoice.payment_failed`
- `payment_intent.payment_failed`
- `customer.subscription.deleted`
- `charge.refunded`
- `charge.dispute.created`

## Services

| Service | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `createPlan({ id, name, amount, interval })`, `plans()` | Define and list plans; `interval` is `month` or `year` |
| `createCheckout({ order_id, customer_id, plan_id })` or `({ order_id, customer_id, amount, description })` | A subscription, or a one-off payment. One checkout per `order_id`: asking again for an open session answers the same session (`reused: true`, no second charge); a paid order is `CONFLICT`. `billing.fraud_signal` runs first |
| `checkout(customer_id, plan_id)` | A subscription checkout whose order is the customer and the plan |
| `getSubscription(customer_id)`, `listInvoices(customer_id)` | Read a customer's state |
| `recordUsage(customer_id, metric, quantity)`, `usage(customer_id, metric, since)` | Metered usage |
| `refund(invoice_id, amount)` | Needs `billing.refund`. Never more than was paid less what was already refunded; the PSP call is idempotent |

Errors are `BillingError` with a code: `INVALID`, `NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `PSP`, `CONFLICT` or `REFUSED`.

## Events and hooks

| Name | Kind | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `billing.checkout_completed` | event | A checkout was paid |
| `billing.payment_received` | event | Money arrived for an invoice |
| `billing.payment_failed` | event | A payment failed; the subscription is now `past_due`. Dunning emails are the app's handler of this event (through `email.send`) |
| `billing.invoice_issued` | event | The PSP issued an invoice; tax-gcc numbers its tax invoice from this (#331) |
| `billing.invoice_paid`, `billing.subscription_changed`, `billing.refunded` | events | Self-explanatory |
| `billing.disputed` | event | A customer disputed a payment with their bank (`charge.dispute.created`): the invoice or one-off order of its payment intent, the amount and Stripe's reason. The invoice row keeps `disputed_at`; the evidence is answered in the Stripe dashboard |
| `billing.fraud_signal` | hook point | Receives `{ customer_id, order_id, amount, currency, mode }` before a checkout session is created. A halt refuses the checkout; the card-testing limits are #123 |

The public view `billing__public_user_plans_v1` (`user_id`, `plan_id`, `status`, `current_period_end`) is what other modules read a user's plan through.

## Pages and roles

| Page | Who | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mount>` | Signed-in users | The plans, the user's subscription and invoices, and **Subscribe** |
| `<mount>/invoices` | Needs `billing.manage` | Every invoice |
| Refund form | Needs `billing.refund` (`r-can`) | Shown on the invoices page |

The default policy (`policies/billing.cedar`):
- `admin` holds both actions;
- `finance` holds `billing.manage` only.

`billing.refund` is sensitive, so every decision on it is audited.

## The adapter

`lib/adapter.ts` defines the adapter interface:
- `createSession`: Stripe's call carries the idempotency key `checkout:<order_id>`;
- `capture`;
- `refund`;
- `parseWebhook`, which normalises the provider's events.

#330 adds the GCC providers behind the same interface.

## Payment methods and adapters (#330)

`config.methods` lists the methods offered, from `card`, `cod` and `bank`; the default is `card`. `createCheckout({ …, method })` refuses a method the app did not enable. `cod` and `bank` are for one-off payments only.

| Method | Adapter | State | Go-live steps (owner) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Card, Stripe UAE | `lib/adapter.ts` `stripe` | Built and tested against recorded request shapes | Stripe account, keys, webhook endpoint (above) |
| Cash on delivery | `src/adapters/offline.ts` | Built. States: `placed` → `out_for_delivery` → `delivered` (paid) or `refused` (unpaid), moved with `codUpdate`, which needs `billing.manage` | None; the courier's confirmation is the app's own call |
| Bank transfer | `src/adapters/offline.ts` | Built. Each order gets a reference `RNX-XXXXXXXX`, shown with `bank_name`, `bank_beneficiary` and `bank_iban` on `<mount>/checkout/pending`. `<mount>/checkout/import` takes the statement as CSV, and `matchTransfer` pays an order only when the reference and the exact amount match. Anything else stays unmatched for a person to check | Fill the bank config; export statements as CSV with `date`, `amount` and `description` columns |
| Checkout.com, Telr, PayTabs, N-Genius | — | **Not built** (#330 stays open): no adapter is written before it can be checked against the provider's sandbox | A merchant account, sandbox credentials, and the webhook secret `BILLING_WEBHOOK_<PROVIDER>_SECRET` per provider |
| Apple Pay and Google Pay | — | **Not built**: they come as payment methods of the card PSPs above | Apple's domain verification file served from the app; Google Pay merchant id |
| Tabby, Tamara (BNPL) | — | **Not built**, including the eligibility rules (amount range, currency) and the rejected path | Merchant account and sandbox with each |

## Owner steps

- A Stripe account, and the live and test keys.
- The webhook endpoint and its signing secret.
- 3DS left on, which is Stripe's default.

## Tests

- `bun test` runs the unit tests on SQLite, with the PSP replaced by a recording stand-in:
  - the Stripe requests, from recorded fixtures;
  - one checkout per order, and the double click;
  - `billing.fraud_signal`;
  - refunds and their limits;
  - every webhook path.
- With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app on the worker:
  - a bad signature gets 401, and a replay is answered `duplicate`;
  - the customer's page;
  - the invoices page per role (none, finance, admin).
- `examples/shop` has the module installed.
